issues.description: The manuscript contains a direct contradiction about when the resistance interventions are delivered. The procedure section states the interventions occur after collaborative recall and after a second filler task, whereas the introduction explicitly states the methods were deliberately placed before collaborative recall to inoculate participants prior to exposure to misinformation. This ambiguity affects the theoretical rationale, internal validity, and replicability because pre-misinformation versus post-misinformation warning/intervention tests fundamentally different mechanisms.
issues.quote: In some other studies concerning the misinformation effect (but not memory conformity) the warning was placed between exposing the original material and the post-event information, or even before the original information (e.g., Greene, Flynn, & Loftus, 1982). In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall (see the rationale for the research below). ... What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation). ... After that, the third phase will take place: it will consist in the procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation that were described above.

issues.description: The manuscript gives incompatible descriptions of the final individual memory test. The methods describe a 20-item open-ended test with confidence ratings and four derived indices, but the analysis plan states that the individual memory test will also use a two-alternative forced-choice format. These are materially different outcome measures with different psychometric and inferential properties. This makes the protocol unreproducible and raises concern about undisclosed analytic flexibility.
issues.quote: Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test... The test will contain 20 open-ended questions... Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test... In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.subcategory: mismatch between hypotheses and manipulation placement
issues.description: The theoretical framework repeatedly argues that the interventions should act on participants who have already noticed discrepancies between their own memory and co-witness information, i.e., after misinformation exposure and discrepancy detection. Yet the manuscript also says the interventions were placed before collaborative recall to inoculate participants. If administered before exposure, the proposed mechanisms involving experienced discrepancy, rejection of consistency assumptions after discussion, and source comparison are not aligned with the intervention timing. This undermines construct validity of the hypothesized mechanisms.
issues.quote: From the above reasoning it follows that our methods of reducing the memory conformity effect are directed towards the participants who are aware of the discrepancy between both the original information and the misinformation obtained from the partner. ... If a person aware of discrepancies was notified of the sources of discrepancies before the individual memory test, there is no reason why they should provide responses in line with the misinformation in that test. ... What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase

issues.description: Participants are tested in pairs, assigned as pairs to condition, and influence each other during collaborative recall. This creates statistical dependence within dyads. However, the analysis plan treats participants as independent observations in repeated-measures ANOVA with N=240 individuals, with no modeling of pair clustering or dyad-level random effects. Ignoring dyadic non-independence can bias standard errors and inflate Type I error.
issues.quote: The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs). ... Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups... The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels ... and one between-subjects factor with four levels

issues.subcategory: power analysis based on inappropriate/unstable effect synthesis
issues.description: The power analysis for replicating memory conformity pools only two studies with highly discrepant effect sizes (g=1.92 and g=0.38), then converts the pooled effect to ANOVA f and uses a correlation of 0.07. A random-effects synthesis from only two studies is unstable, and the resulting pooled effect is not reliable for planning. Moreover, the source studies may differ in outcome definitions and design details. This likely yields an overoptimistic estimate of power.
issues.quote: The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges’ g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020). Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13. This amounts to a Cohen f of about 0.57.

issues.description: The manuscript converts a pooled Hedges' g into Cohen's f for repeated-measures ANOVA without explaining the conversion or assumptions. Such conversions depend on design specifics and covariance structure; without transparency, the power analysis is not reproducible and may be incorrect.
issues.quote: The joint effect size, which was 1.13. This amounts to a Cohen f of about 0.57.

issues.description: The power analysis treats the sample as 240 participants, but randomization is at the pair level and observations are nested within pairs. Effective sample size is therefore closer to the number of pairs, depending on intraclass correlation. The reported power is likely overstated.
issues.quote: Considering the accessible financial, organizational and time resources, a sample of 240 participants was assumed; this allows for excellent power to detect medium and large effect sizes but not small ones.

issues.description: The three intervention conditions are not matched on content, modality, and complexity. Demonstration and motivation includes a DRM false memory task, direct individualized feedback, and a motivational podcast; Extended warning and Education are each a single approximately 7-minute podcast; the control is a generic soft-skills podcast. Any observed differences could reflect differential engagement, task demand, arousal, self-relevance, feedback, or cognitive load rather than the intended constructs. This compromises causal interpretation between interventions.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... First, in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used... The results will be fed back to participants... Next, the participants’ motivation... will consist in them listening to a podcast... In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: No manipulation checks are specified for whether participants attended to, understood, believed, or were affected by the interventions. Without checks, null or positive findings cannot be interpreted: failure may reflect ineffective delivery rather than theoretical falsification, and positive effects cannot be linked to the intended mechanisms.
issues.quote: Each method will be applied in a different group of subjects; the fourth group will be the control. ... The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA...

issues.subcategory: key moderator hypothesized but not measured
issues.description: The authors' theoretical account hinges on participants being aware of discrepancies between their own memory and the partner's report, yet no direct measure of discrepancy awareness or source-monitoring awareness is specified. Therefore, the central mechanism cannot be tested, and intervention effects cannot be examined in the subgroup for whom the theory predicts efficacy.
issues.quote: Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.subcategory: failure to operationalize misinformation exposure correctly
issues.description: The plan ultimately treats all discussed critical items as having contained misinformation regardless of what the partner actually said. This is conceptually wrong because some discussions may not introduce discrepant misinformation: the partner may guess the participant's correct answer, say 'don't know,' fail to state the discrepant detail, or the pair may not exchange the critical value effectively. Classifying all discussed items as misinformation-exposed introduces outcome misclassification and attenuates or biases the effect.
issues.quote: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s differing version of events.

issues.description: The analysis plan first defines misleading exposure based on what the partner actually said during discussion, then immediately states all discussed items will be categorized as having contained misinformation. These are incompatible coding schemes that could produce different results. This ambiguity creates major analytic flexibility and undermines preregistration clarity.
issues.quote: All the answers provided by the partner during the discussion ... are misleading the participant and will be classified as misleading. However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen ... the situation will not be classified as misleading. ... In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions ... we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation

issues.description: The MORI stimulus is described as containing eight critical details, but the collaborative recognition test includes only four critical questions and all pairs discuss the same four critical details. The manuscript does not clearly state how the remaining four critical details are selected as non-discussed controls, nor whether item order and item assignment are counterbalanced. This matters because discussed and non-discussed items may differ intrinsically in memorability.
issues.quote: Both versions are identical except for eight critical details... The test will comprise 12 questions, four of which refer to critical details... In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.description: The design section claims discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, but the procedure states all pairs discuss the same set of four critical details. Both cannot be true unless there is item-set counterbalancing not described. Without actual counterbalancing, item effects are confounded with discussion status.
issues.quote: In the study, the memory conformity effect will be measured in a within-subjects design and discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced. ... In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.subcategory: inappropriate use of ANOVA for count/proportion outcomes
issues.description: Primary outcomes are counts of correct, misinformation-consistent, and other answers over a small fixed number of critical items. Such bounded count/proportion data are unlikely to satisfy normality and homoscedasticity assumptions of ANOVA, especially with values from 0 to 4 or 0 to 8. More appropriate analyses would use generalized mixed models (e.g., binomial) at the item level with random effects for participant and item. Using ANOVA may yield inefficient or biased inference.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers ... We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices

issues.description: The manuscript proposes analyzing four indices from the memory test plus average accuracy on filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions, plus follow-up pairwise comparisons and exploratory DRM prediction analyses, but specifies no correction for multiple testing. This increases false-positive risk and allows selective emphasis on significant findings.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices... Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions... In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed. As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor

issues.description: The power analysis assumes directional significance tests for planned comparisons, but the analysis plan does not state one-tailed tests, preregister the precise one-sided hypotheses for each comparison, or justify them. This discrepancy may inflate apparent power and introduces ambiguity in inferential thresholds.
issues.quote: For the planned comparisons between two groups ... the required sample sizes are 492, 82, and 34 participants, respectively. Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.

issues.description: The manuscript says pairs will be randomly assigned to groups but gives no details on sequence generation, allocation concealment, block sizes, stratification, or implementation. Because pair characteristics could affect conformity, lack of randomization detail reduces reproducibility and raises risk of allocation bias.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups

issues.subcategory: no blinding and risk of experimenter expectancy
issues.description: The experimenter appears to administer condition-specific podcasts and the DRM feedback and also records responses. No blinding procedures are described. Especially in the DRM condition, the experimenter explicitly tells participants they were fooled and urges them to rely on their own memory, which may create expectancy or differential demand characteristics.
issues.quote: At this moment in this group, the experimenter will give the following information to the participants: “Thank you for completing this memory task... You can see how easily human memory can be distorted”. ... The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory

issues.description: The interventions, especially Extended warning and Demonstration and motivation, explicitly tell participants about misinformation, deception, and the desirability of using only their own memory. Any reduction in misinformation responses may reflect demand compliance or response strategy shifts rather than true resistance to memory conformity. No procedures are described to distinguish memory change from strategic responding.
issues.quote: The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory, not on any information stemming from the partner. ... It will also provide information about the misinformation effect, source misattribution, and the influence of a lack of confidence on memory reports

issues.description: The authors assert that normative influence is completely ruled out because the final test is individual. This is too strong. Normative pressures can operate during the discussion phase and can alter later recall, confidence, source monitoring, or willingness to disagree privately. Dismissing normative influence narrows interpretation unjustifiably and weakens the conceptual framework.
issues.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study

issues.description: The manuscript proposes distinct efficacy ranking and mechanisms for the three interventions despite substantial acknowledged overlap and no measures of proposed mediators such as confidence, source monitoring, metacognition, vigilance, or motivation. Ranking efficacy without mechanistic measurement is speculative and difficult to interpret.
issues.quote: we tentatively assume that the most effective technique... will be Demonstration and motivation... Extended warning... slightly less effective... more effective than Education about memory... Secondly, we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions

issues.subcategory: possible testing/interference effect of DRM manipulation
issues.description: The DRM false memory induction is itself a memory task with feedback immediately before the main eyewitness memory test. This may differentially affect general memory confidence, fatigue, source monitoring, mood, or strategy, independently of the intended 'demonstration and motivation' mechanism. Because other groups do not perform a comparable task, the condition is not a clean manipulation.
issues.quote: First... a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used... The subjects will also receive a worksheet... The results will be fed back to participants... Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity... they will complete the individual memory test

issues.subcategory: intervention duration and equivalence not fully specified
issues.description: Only the two podcast interventions are described as approximately 7 minutes. The DRM-based condition likely takes longer due to list presentation, written recall, feedback, and subsequent podcast, but no duration is specified. Unequal exposure time and task burden across conditions could affect results.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast... First... a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used... Next, the participants’ motivation... will consist in them listening to a podcast

issues.description: The content of the podcasts and DRM lists are described only broadly; exact scripts, wording, audio characteristics, list items, list order, scoring rules, and language adaptation are not provided. This impairs reproducibility and leaves room for post hoc tailoring.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast about the fallibility of human memory... The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast discussing the mechanisms of memory... Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect.

issues.subcategory: selection of strongest DRM lists may capitalize on prior results
issues.description: The DRM materials are chosen because they 'produce the strongest effect' based on previous research, but no criteria, sample, language validation, or preregistered selection process is provided. This can capitalize on chance and may maximize the manipulation at the expense of comparability or generalizability.
issues.quote: Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect.

issues.subcategory: exploratory predictor underpowered and conceptually unclear
issues.description: Using DRM performance as a predictor of MORI susceptibility is only mentioned briefly without specifying the model, outcome, covariates, or theoretical relation. Given the nested design and limited reliability of short DRM measures, such exploratory analyses are likely underpowered and hard to interpret.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.description: Only technical problems are listed as grounds for exclusion. No criteria are given for failure to follow instructions, peeking over glasses, inability to perceive the display, hearing problems for podcasts, prior familiarity with the MORI/DRM paradigms, non-native language proficiency, or suspicion about the deception. Such omissions threaten internal validity and analytic discretion.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.subcategory: no plan for handling missing data
issues.description: The manuscript does not specify what will happen if participants omit answers on the open-ended test, fail to provide confidence ratings, or if one member of a pair is lost. Because outcomes are counts over items and dyads are interdependent, missing data handling matters for bias and reproducibility.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test... We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.description: Pairs are formed from volunteers but no information is provided on whether pair members are strangers, acquaintances, friends, or matched on sex/age. Prior work shows relationship variables can affect memory conformity. Without controlling or recording pair familiarity and related characteristics, an important source of variability/confounding remains unaddressed.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.subcategory: broad age range without analytic control
issues.description: The sample spans ages 16 to 35, including minors and adults with potentially different cognitive, social, and legal-response characteristics. The rationale only addresses avoiding young-old pairings, but age within this range may still affect conformity and intervention response. No stratification or covariate plan is provided.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; ... The age of the participants will be restricted in order to avoid a situation in which a very young participant would discuss the original material with an elderly one

issues.subcategory: inclusion of minors without consent details
issues.description: Participants as young as 16 are included, yet no ethical procedures for parental consent/assent or protections for minors are described. Given deception and discussion of wrongful convictions, ethical oversight details are important.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old

issues.description: The manuscript provides no information on institutional ethics approval or informed consent procedures despite using deception, audio recording, and potentially minors. This is a significant reporting omission.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded. ... Finally, the participants will be debriefed.

issues.subcategory: audio recording purpose not integrated into analysis
issues.description: Collaborative recall discussions are audio recorded, but no coding scheme, reliability assessment, or planned use of these recordings is specified beyond documenting disagreement. Given that actual exposure to misinformation is central, failure to analyze discussion content wastes a critical validity resource.
issues.quote: The discussion will be audio recorded.

issues.subcategory: no check that MORI deception succeeded
issues.description: The MORI technique depends on participants believing they saw the same film and complying with the glasses instructions. The protocol does not include a preregistered manipulation check for awareness of dual versions or peeking/noncompliance. Without this, failed deception could dilute or distort the effect.
issues.quote: Thanks to polarized glasses ... each of them sees a different movie version while being convinced that they are actually watching the same movie clip. ... Please make sure you watch the movie through the glasses (no peeking over the top or around the side)

issues.description: If the final test is open-ended, the manuscript does not specify who will code responses, whether coders are blind to condition, how synonyms/partially correct responses will be handled, or inter-rater reliability. These details are essential for reproducibility and to prevent bias.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions... Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers ... (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers

issues.subcategory: confidence ratings collected but no analysis plan
issues.description: Participants provide 0–100% confidence ratings for each answer, yet no confirmatory or exploratory analysis of confidence is specified. Given the theoretical emphasis on confidence, trust in memory, and metacognition, omitting a plan for these data is a missed opportunity and suggests incomplete preregistration.
issues.quote: for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% ... to 100%

issues.description: Multiple possible endpoints are proposed—correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, overall number of answers, average accuracy on several item types, and difference scores—but no primary outcome is designated. Lack of a primary endpoint increases researcher degrees of freedom and complicates interpretation.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived... We will explore ... using all four indices... Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions.

issues.description: The introduction states the MORI technique brings laboratory conditions closer to real-life witness discussion. However, the study uses a short silent film, artificial discussion prompts, and explicit interventions. The ecological validity claim is overstated and may mislead readers about generalizability to actual eyewitness contexts.
issues.quote: The main reason for its popularity is the fact that the MORI technique brings laboratory conditions closer to the real-life situations in which witnesses discuss a crime and are then individually interviewed by law enforcement officers.

issues.subcategory: control condition may not be inert or matched
issues.description: The control podcast concerns 'soft skills related to social attitudes,' but no rationale is given for why this is neutral with respect to memory, confidence, social influence, or motivation. Depending on content, it could affect social conformity or attentional engagement. Also, it may not be matched to the DRM condition's activity level.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The efficacy criterion is defined as a smaller difference between discussed and non-discussed accuracy in intervention groups versus control. Difference scores can conflate baseline memory differences and intervention effects on both discussed and non-discussed items. A more informative model would test item-level accuracy with fixed effects and interactions. The current plan risks ambiguous interpretation, especially if interventions alter overall memory performance.
issues.quote: The efficacy of a given method will be confirmed if the magnitude of memory conformity (expressed as the difference between the accuracy on discussed and non-discussed items) is smaller in the group in which this method was applied than in the control group.

issues.subcategory: possible order and fatigue effects not controlled
issues.description: All participants complete tasks in the same order, with interventions immediately before the final memory test. There is no mention of counterbalancing test item order or controlling for fatigue/recency. This is particularly relevant because interventions differ in cognitive demand and duration, potentially affecting subsequent recall independent of conformity resistance.
issues.quote: Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test

issues.subcategory: timeline indicates protocol status, not completed study
issues.description: The manuscript appears to be a proposal/registered report stage 1 rather than a completed empirical study, yet it is framed as a manuscript for review. There are no actual results, and many sections use future tense ('will be used', 'planned'). This is not necessarily a flaw if submitted as a protocol, but the status should be explicit because evidential claims cannot be assessed as findings.
issues.quote: The main goal of this proposal is to analyze... ... The study will be conducted in 2023. If the Stage 1 review is accepted

issues.subcategory: insufficient details on collaborative recall scoring
issues.description: The collaborative recognition test allows pairs 60 seconds per question and documents both responses if they disagree, but the manuscript does not explain how disagreements, multiple utterances, uncertainty, or dominant-partner effects will be coded for misinformation exposure. Given the centrality of discussion content, this lack of scoring detail hampers validity.
issues.quote: Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer. If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented.

issues.subcategory: forced discussion of same items may create item-specific confounds
issues.description: Having all pairs discuss the same four critical details may ensure exposure but also confounds discussion status with the specific content of those items. If some details are more memorable or more easily contaminated, the discussed/non-discussed comparison may reflect item differences rather than misinformation effects unless true counterbalancing is implemented.
issues.quote: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.subcategory: education intervention may plausibly increase suggestibility yet no safeguards
issues.description: The authors acknowledge that teaching memory fallibility could reduce confidence and increase suggestibility, but provide no design feature to disentangle beneficial metacognitive awareness from harmful confidence reduction. Because confidence is central to their theory, this omission limits interpretability of null or adverse effects.
issues.quote: presenting participants with research confirming the fallibility of memory may result in decreased confidence in their own memory, which, in turn, might result in increased suggestibility... If this is the case, increased memory conformity is possible.

issues.subcategory: language and transcription errors affecting clarity
issues.description: There are multiple wording errors that create ambiguity in key methodological sections, such as inconsistent terminology ('familarised', 'in in', 'accuracy on the filler'), which may indicate insufficient proofreading of the protocol. While minor individually, in aggregate they reduce precision in a preregistered methods document.
issues.quote: participants first are familarised... those in in the ‘Education about memory’ group... we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions
